THE GENERATOR IS EDGE-DRIVEN WITH ABSOLUTE DELAYS
not woken once per clock. A 2.6 M clock testbench that
woke up 2.6 M times to decide whether the pin had moved
would spend its wall time deciding it had not.
read the COUNTER, not the flag
60 clocks = exactly 1 us.
Port 0x4.
NOT port 0x7 (STATUS), WHICH IS 260 CLOCKS = 4.33 us
the UART half-bit tick, which exists to place a serial
sample mid-cell. The first version counted it and
measured
0.24 ticks per microsecond
, reporting a
200 us period as 46. A tick counter whose name says
TIMER is not a microsecond.
now
elapsed = (now - dmem[7]) mod 256
THERE IS NO FLAG TO LOSE, AND THAT IS WHY THE
COUNTER IS READ RATHER THAN THE FLAG.
A clear-on-read flag is ONE BIT, so a poll loop that takes
longer than a tick reports several ticks as one, and the
loss is invisible in the result - the measurement is
simply short, by an amount that depends on how busy the
program was. This program is one instruction from that
defect and does not have it.
Exact for any loop up to 255 us, and this loop is
1.3 us
- two hundred times inside it.
T += elapsed (16-bit add)
the rising edge: the design decision
dmem[4] != 0x40 and the pad is high
T = 0, H = 0 - BOTH counters reset
THE PERIOD IS T AT THE RISING EDGE, BECAUSE T IS RESET
AT EVERY RISING EDGE. THE HIGH TIME IS H AT THE RISING
EDGE, BECAUSE H IS ALSO RESET THERE AND STOPS COUNTING
AT THE FALLING EDGE.
TWO RESETS REMOVE EVERY 16-BIT SUBTRACT, EVERY COMPARE
AND EVERY DIVIDE. And this machine has no carry flag,
so a 16-bit subtract is a four-case analysis on bit 7 and
a compare is the same analysis again. There is none of
either in the program, and that is the design rather than a
limitation worked around.
The commit message called this act "capture only" before a
line of it existed, and that is what it turned out to be,
for a reason the commit message could not have known.
the high time: the falling edge only STOPS the counter
the line goes LOW
H stops counting here
Nothing to subtract. The accumulator simply stops, and at
the NEXT rising edge whatever is in H is the high time of
the period that just ended.
the 16-bit add, and the guard it does not need
THREE ARITHMETIC FACTS DECIDED THE WHOLE PROGRAM.
A 16-bit INCREMENT IS CHEAP.
+1 on the low byte is exactly
zero when it carries, so the carry test is one JZ on the
low result.
A 16-BIT ADD OF A VARIABLE IS AFFORDABLE, BUT ONLY JUST.
The carry test is the same JZ, except that 0 + 0 = 0 is
not a carry, so a general addend needs a GUARD: when the
low result is zero, reload the low operand and test it
for zero too.
This program gets that guard away FOR FREE,
because its
addend is the elapsed microsecond count and is therefore
NEVER ZERO - "the low byte came out zero" can then only
mean "the low byte wrapped". The guard is not skipped, it
is UNNECESSARY, and the comment says which. A program
adding two memory values would need it.
A 16-BIT SUBTRACT IS A DIFFERENT MACHINE,
and point 3 is
why this program contains none.
the bank, every third period
every 3 periods, bank (T, H) into the slot dmem[5] names
THE FIRST PERIOD OF EACH RUN IS A WARM-UP AND IS NOT
CHECKED, for a reason that is a property of the PROTOCOL
and not of the firmware: the firmware starts in the middle
of it, so the time since the previous rising edge is not a
period.
A receiver that starts mid-period misses that one period,
and a testbench that pretended otherwise would be asking the
firmware to measure something it was never present for.
T high H low into dmem[slot*2 .. slot*2+1]
dmem[5] DOUBLES AS THE "NOT STARTED YET" STATE (FF),
because the program needed one byte more than the machine
has and the slot index is the one value that is not a
measurement. The map uses all sixteen bytes and one byte is
shared rather than found.
the accuracy the instrument actually has
Every banked point, checked against a SECOND, INDEPENDENT
measurement of the pad - the receiver in the TB, not
the generator's table. A generator that knew the answer
would agree with a firmware that had the sweep wrong.
point
period
high
duty
[pad]
EVERY PERIOD IS EXACT EXCEPT THREE, BY EXACTLY ONE TICK
801 and 399 against 10 000, 800 and 400 - and the duty follows to a tenth
of a point because the two counts share the same edge discipline.
THAT IS THE RESOLUTION SHOWING UP IN THE LOG INSTEAD OF HIDING IN A
TOLERANCE, which is what a measured-truth record should look like.
WHY THE TOLERANCE IS PER POINT AND NOT ONE NUMBER.
The instrument's resolution IS the specification:
point
period
relative error of a 1 us counter
100 us (10 kHz)
So the tolerance is 1 % of the period with a floor of 1.5 ticks. At the fast
end of the sweep the TOLERANCE is the dominant term and the quantisation is a
percent of it.
A single accuracy number would be a false claim at one end or
the other, and that is why the act states per point.
The 16-bit claim is point 1: 10 001 us, from a counter whose low byte wrapped
39 TIMES. A firmware counting into a byte reports 16 us there, and has no
symptom at any other point in the sweep.
